known_facts_book1: A little slice taken off the Quadling Country and therefore really a part of the Land of Oz, though Oz people know nothing of it except what Glinda's Record Book says.
Is separated from the rest of the Quadling Country by a row of mountains too steep to climb, at whose foot lies a wide, deep gulf supposed to be impassable.
Is on the Map of Oz, but is ruled by its own King instead of by Ozma, and the laws of Oz are not obeyed there.
Most of its people are good but very timid, living in constant fear of their fierce ruler and of several Wicked Witches.
Its people have never before seen a stranger; Trot, Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright are the first that ever came.
Ends the book ruled by Queen Gloria with Pon as her Royal Consort, with the deposed Krewl as the castle's gardener's boy.

known_relations_book1.King Krewl: Its usurping ruler, deposed by the Orks.
known_relations_book1.Gloria: Its rightful heir and finally its crowned Queen.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler of Oz to whom it owes allegiance without knowing it.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: The Sorceress who learns of it only through her Record Book.

known_facts_book1: A country where the Ork lands the travellers after the flight from Pessim's island, entirely unknown to Trot and Cap'n Bill.
Has no water at all; it rains lemonade instead, which is caught in jars and considered refreshing and healthful.
Its snow is popcorn — crisp, slightly warm, nicely salted and buttered — and falls in flakes so large and queer that Trot does not recognize it.
All its winds and breezes are perfumed: south is violets, north is wild roses, east is lilies-of-the-valley, west is lilac, so no weathervane is needed.
All the birds of Mo are educated to talk, and they gather in flocks to eat the popcorn snow.
Is home to the Bumpy Man, the Mountain Ear, who lives on the flat top of a high mountain.
Is the country the Wise Donkey of the earlier tome came from, though that is not mentioned here.

known_relations_book1.the Bumpy Man: Its Mountain Ear, who keeps the mountain steady.
known_relations_book1.Button-Bright: Found buried in its popcorn snow.
known_relations_book1.Cap'n Bill: Who catches and enlarges three of its birds to carry the party away.

known_facts_book1: A small island reached through a shaft the Ork flies up out of, after the tunnel from the cavern under the sea.
Bears melons, cherries, wild plums, walnuts, filberts, almonds and chestnuts, so no one need starve there.
Grows a bush of lavender berries about the size of gooseberries which shrink whoever eats one to about two inches high.
Grows on the east side a small tree of dark purple berries which restore the eater to full size — the antidote, and the trees grow nowhere else in all the world.
Is inhabited only by Pessim, who was left there alone by his neighbors.
Is left behind by the Ork carrying Trot and Cap'n Bill, shrunken, in Trot's sunbonnet tied round his neck.

known_relations_book1.Pessim: Its only inhabitant, who calls himself its King.
known_relations_book1.the Ork: Who shrinks there by accident and is restored there.
known_relations_book1.Trot: Who shrinks deliberately to be carried away in her own sunbonnet.

known_facts_book1: A wide, deep gulf at the foot of the mountains that separate Jinxland from the rest of the Quadling Country, said to have no bottom.
Is the gulf into which King Kynd, Gloria's father, fell and was never seen again.
Is what Googly-Goo proposes throwing Pon into.
Is crossed by the Scarecrow on two strands spun across it by a spider fed two of Glinda's magic pills, one strand walked on and one held for balance.

known_facts_book1: The Great Waterfall is the highest in all the Land of Oz, a sheet of silver dropping into a tiny lake that seems to have no outlet.
Behind the sheet of water is a cave reached along the wet rocks, and inside it a series of steps cut down into the rock.
The cavern's walls and domed roof are lined with countless cut rubies that light the whole place with a radiant red glow.
In its center the river rises again in a bubbling caldron whose spray takes the ruby color and looks like a seething mass of flame.
A broad ledge covered with rubies runs all around the cavern to where the river plunges finally underground.
Is where the Scarecrow surfaces twice after falling over the waterfall, and where Cap'n Bill hooks him out with his wooden leg.

known_relations_book1.Scarecrow: Who falls over the fall and is fished out of the cavern pool.
known_relations_book1.Button-Bright: Who spots the cave behind the waterfall.

known_facts_book1: The country the Orks come from, where they are the absolute rulers of all living things from ants to elephants.
Its location is unknown even to the Ork for most of the book; he loses all track of distance and direction searching for it.
Is found at last not far from Jinxland, on the far side of the great sandy desert.
Welcomes the Ork's return so royally that a great celebration is held in his honor, delaying his return to his friends.
Sends fifty Orks to Jinxland at his call, and expects him back for a surprise party on his uncle.
Is never entered by any of the human characters and is described only in the Ork's own words.
